alloys.description: Newly designed carbon-free, austenite-based low-density steel in which part of the Al of the Fe-Mn-Al-C system is replaced by Ti and the entire C is replaced by B, prepared as a 50 kg cast ingot by vacuum induction melting; designed to combine a low density with a high Young's modulus and good strength-ductility via a heterogeneous δ-ferrite + austenite + TiB2 triplex microstructure.

paper.paper_scope: The study designs and produces a new carbon-free, austenite-based low-density triplex steel (Fe-15.5Mn-3.95Al-5Ti-2.15B wt.%) by conventional hot rolling, achieving low density (6.88 g/cm3), high Young's modulus (225 GPa) and an improved strength-ductility balance through heterogeneous δ-ferrite bands plus micron-sized TiB2 particles, and compares it with a conventional Fe-TiB2 steel and an interstitial-free steel using experiments and finite-element simulation.
paper.title: Low-density and high-modulus steel achieved by hypereutectic TiB2 and high Al ferrite phase

processes.description: Ingot homogenized at 1373 K for 2 h, then hot rolled in the two-phase region in five rolling steps with a finishing temperature of 1173 K to produce a 3 mm thick sheet, followed by air cooling to room temperature, giving the as-hot-rolled heterogeneous δ-ferrite + austenite + TiB2 microstructure.
processes.processes_notes: This is the single fabrication/terminal state of the present steel studied in the paper (initial undeformed and post-tensile-deformation states are characterization points of the same as-hot-rolled material).

unmapped_findings: The present steel's microstructure is a heterogeneous triplex: a fully equiaxed austenite matrix (~62 vol.%) with elongated δ-ferrite bands (~26 vol.%) and micron-sized TiB2 particles (~12.5 vol.% by XRD; particle sizes 2.4-35 µm, average 15 µm).
Measured physical and mechanical properties of the present steel: density 6.88 g cm-3, Young's modulus 225 GPa, specific modulus 32.7 GPa g-1 cm3, σy 503 MPa, σu 672 MPa, uniform elongation 13%.
The chemical compositions of the two reference steels (conventional Fe-TiB2 steel and interstitial-free steel) are reported only in Supplementary Table S1 and are not available in the main text.
